# CopySync

> CopySync is a free, open-source (MIT) app for macOS and Windows that syncs the clipboard and files between computers: copy on one, paste on another — Mac to Mac, Mac to Windows, or Windows to Windows. It works across different accounts and different networks. Devices connect peer-to-peer over WebRTC with end-to-end DTLS encryption; when a direct connection fails, traffic is relayed through a TURN server the user hosts themselves. The server stores no accounts and cannot read clipboard content.
>
> CopySync 是一款免费开源（MIT）的 macOS 与 Windows 工具，在两台电脑之间同步剪贴板与文件：一台复制，另一台直接粘贴，Mac 与 Windows 互通。不要求同一个账号，跨网络可用。设备间 WebRTC 直连、DTLS 端到端加密，打不通时经用户自建服务器的 TURN 中转；服务器不存账号，看不到复制内容。

Key facts:

- Current version: 1.2.0, released 2026-10-09. Adds the Windows client.
- Mac client: macOS 13 Ventura or later, universal binary for Intel and Apple silicon. Distributed as a DMG; not notarized by Apple, so the first launch needs "Open Anyway" in System Settings → Privacy & Security.
- Windows client: Windows 10 (21H2+) and Windows 11, x64. Per-user installer (CopySync-Setup.exe, no admin rights) or portable zip; not code-signed, so SmartScreen needs "More info → Run anyway" once. Runs in the notification area; pasted files are real files usable in Explorer, WeChat and Office. Skips content that password managers mark as sensitive.
- Server: a single static Go binary for Linux (x86_64, ARM64) or macOS, installed via systemd script or Docker Compose. Ports: 8787/tcp (signaling), 3478/udp (STUN/TURN), 32768–60999/udp (relay).
- Content synced: plain text, rich text (HTML plus a plain-text copy), images, files, folders.
- Works on multi-uplink networks (e.g. offices with two ISPs) that pick an uplink per destination: the client probes several STUN servers from one shared port to learn its address on every uplink and sends all of them to the peer. Diagnose with `copysync-cli nat`. If a connection lands on the relay first, the client retries the direct path with an ICE restart while idle.
- Items under 50 MB (adjustable 1 MB–1 GB) are pushed on copy; larger files sync as a record and are pulled on demand.
- History keeps 3 days by default (adjustable 1 hour–30 days).
- Pairing: 6-character code valid for 5 minutes, plus a human check that both devices show the same two fingerprints (one per device's Ed25519 public key), which prevents man-in-the-middle attacks by the server.
- Not supported: iPhone/iPad (iOS forbids background clipboard monitoring). The server stores nothing: while the other computer is unreachable, the latest 20 items are kept in memory and sent when it reconnects (added to its history, not its clipboard).
- Compared with Apple's Universal Clipboard: no same-Apple-ID or proximity requirement, keeps a history, handles large files and folders.
